summary: Digitizing microfilm involves more than scanning. Learn the security questions every organization should ask before starting a micrographics conversion…
body_markdown:
#### Why You Should Go Beyond Sample Images


When organizations evaluate microfilm conversion providers, they often focus on three things:


1. Sample Images
2. Price
3. Turnaround time


Those factors matter, but they don't tell the whole story. A few good sample images don't necessarily indicate a quality process. The real question is: ***How does a provider consistently produce accurate, complete, and reliable results across an entire collection?*** The answer lies in quality management.


#### Quality Is More Than Image Resolution


Many buyers assume quality is simply a matter of resolution. While resolution is important, it's only one piece of the puzzle.


A successful conversion project depends on:


- Image quality
- Density and contrast
- Completeness
- Film handling
- Inspection procedures
- Quality Assurance (QA)
- Quality Control (QC)


An image can meet resolution requirements and still be difficult to read if the film was poorly handled, improperly exposed, or inadequately inspected. The goal isn't just to create images. It's to create reliable digital records.


#### Quality Starts Before Scanning


In our previous article,[Your Microfilm Isn't the Only Thing at Risk](https://intellinetics.com/company/resources/your-microfilm-isnt-the-only-thing-at-risk) , we discussed how successful projects depend on inventory, preparation, scanning, quality assurance, indexing, and preservation.


Quality begins before the scanner is ever turned on. Film should be inspected for:


- Damage
- Dirt and debris
- Deterioration
- Missing or mislabeled reels
- Unusual formats


Collections showing signs of Vinegar Syndrome or Redox may require special handling. If you haven't evaluated the health of your collection, our article[Is Your Microfilm in a Pickle...or Does It Just Smell That Way?](https://intellinetics.com/company/resources/is-your-microfilm-in-a-pickle-or-does-it-just-smell-that-way) explains common warning signs and preservation risks.
